what_its_for: Hydroxyzine is used to help relieve anxiety and tension, treat itching caused by allergic reactions, and help you feel calm or sleepy before or after surgery or other medical procedures. It works by blocking certain natural chemicals in your body that cause these symptoms.
how_to_take: Take hydroxyzine exactly as your doctor prescribed. You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a meal or snack. If you are using the liquid form, carefully measure your dose using the special measuring spoon or cup that came with the medicine — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Swallow capsules or tablets whole with a full glass of water.
dosing: Your dose will depend on your age, weight, and what you are being treated for. For anxiety in adults, a common dose is 50 to 100 mg up to 4 times a day. For itching in adults, a common dose is 25 mg 3 to 4 times a day. For children, the dose is based on body weight and will be determined by your doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never take more than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store hydroxyzine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking hydroxyzine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness and may be dangerous. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medicines that cause drowsiness, such as sleep aids, muscle relaxers, or other anxiety medicines, unless your doctor approves. Tell your doctor about all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you are taking.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a fast, irregular, or pounding heartbeat; severe dizziness or fainting; difficulty breathing; seizures; confusion or unusual behavior; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat. Also contact your doctor if your symptoms do not improve or get worse.
when_it_works: Hydroxyzine works fairly quickly. You may start to feel its effects within 15 to 30 minutes after taking it. The full effect usually lasts for 4 to 6 hours. It does not need to build up in your system over time like some other medicines.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with caution. Elderly patients are more sensitive to the drowsy and dizzy effects of hydroxyzine, which can increase the risk of falls. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Hydroxyzine is generally not recommended during the first trimester of pregnancy. Breastfeeding: It is not known if hydroxyzine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while on this medicine. Children: Dosing is based on the child's weight and will be determined by the doctor. Keep this medicine out of reach of children.
